title: Child marriage before 18, SDG regions compared, by location
headline: Central and Southern Asia: child marriage down 22.7 points since 2005
subtitle: Percentage of women (aged 20-24 years) married or in union before age 18
years: Central and S. Asia: from 47.3% in 2005 to 24.6% in 2025. World: from 24.2% to 18.5%.
data_line: Data: UNICEF via UN SDG Global Database, series SP_DYN_MRBF18, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Central and Southern Asia: child marriage down 22.7 points since 2005. Central and S. Asia: from 47.3% in 2005 to 24.6% in 2025. World: from 24.2% to 18.5%. Sub-Saharan Africa: 38.3% in 2005 to 30.7% in 2025; N. Africa and W. Asia: 18.5% in 2005 to 15.3% in 2025; Central and S. Asia: 47.3% in 2005 to 24.6% in 2025; E. and S.-E. Asia: 9.4% in 2005 to 7.6% in 2025; Latin America, Caribbean: 21.0% in 2005 to 18.4% in 2025; Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ): 25.1% in 2005 to 24.9% in 2025; World: 24.2% in 2005 to 18.5% in 2025
question: What lies behind the change in child marriage in Central and Southern Asia, and what could others learn from it?
